<span class="eyebrow">What it is</span>

## If you already use Quarto, you already know Hub

Hub does not change how Quarto works. It changes who can be in the file with you.

::: {.card-grid}
::: {.hub-card}
<span class="eyebrow">Edit together</span>

### One project, many cursors
Everyone on the link edits the same files at the same time. Changes merge as you type. No branches, no "who has the latest version."
:::
::: {.hub-card}
<span class="eyebrow">Preview as you type</span>

### Rendered output, live
The preview pane re-renders in the browser while you write, for documents, websites, and revealjs slides.
:::
::: {.hub-card}
<span class="eyebrow">Share a link</span>

### Reviewers need nothing
Authors sign in with Google to create projects. Reviewers open the share link and read or comment. No account, no install.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**People and agents in the same file.** Hub is built so that anything with access to a project, a teammate or an AI agent, edits the same source and shows up in the same history. See [Coming soon](#coming-soon) for where agent support stands.
:::

:::
:::

::: {.content-block}

<span class="eyebrow">Today</span>

## Best today for markdown-first work

Hub is a preview. It is already the fastest way to write these things with other people:

::: {.card-grid}
::: {.hub-card}
### Websites and docs
Multi-page Quarto websites with a shared file tree, outline, and preview. Good for team docs, handbooks, and project sites.
:::
::: {.hub-card}
### Meeting notes
A running `.qmd` per team that everyone types into during the call. Rendered notes, no cleanup afterward.
:::
::: {.hub-card}
### Presentations
revealjs decks, co-authored and previewed in place. Hand the link to a co-presenter instead of emailing a PDF.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
**Why this matters if you use quarto-cli.** Collaboration today means Git and pull requests for authors, and Word or PDF exports for everyone else. Hub replaces that with one link. Nothing to relearn; the collaboration is the new part.
:::

:::

::: {.content-block}

<span class="eyebrow">Built on Quarto 2</span>

## The engine underneath

Hub renders in the browser because of Quarto 2, a rewrite of the Quarto engine in Rust that is fast enough to re-render a document as you type. Hub is the collaborative experience; Q2 is the engine that makes it possible.

::: {.stack-row}
<div class="stack-name">Quarto Hub</div>
<p>The shared editor and hosting. Where people and agents work on a project together.</p>
:::
::: {.stack-row}
<div class="stack-name">Quarto 2</div>
<p>The next-generation rendering engine. Runs natively and in the browser. Experimental, under active development.</p>
:::
::: {.stack-row}
<div class="stack-name">`quarto-cli`</div>
<p>Quarto 1, the tool you use today. It keeps working exactly as it does; Hub does not replace it.</p>
:::

:::

### Try it
Open [quarto-hub.com](https://quarto-hub.com), sign in with Google, and create a project. Share the link with one other person and edit the same paragraph.
:::
::: {.hub-card}
### Tell us what breaks
Hub is a preview. If a project that renders with quarto-cli does not open cleanly in Hub, [file an issue](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-hub/issues) and include the project.
:::
